issues.title: Cross-field validation using field_validator incorrectly
issues.description: The validation logic checks both bucket_folder and bucket fields (cross-field validation) but uses @field_validator instead of @model_validator, causing order-dependent validation issues and accessing potentially unvalidated fields via info.data
issues.rule_name: Pydantic Models Must Use model_validator for Cross-Field Validation

issues.title: Incorrect string matching for path prefix detection causes false positives
issues.description: The double-nesting prevention logic uses `self.bucket_folder in path` instead of `path.startswith(self.bucket_folder)`. This causes false positives when bucket_folder appears anywhere in the path, not just as a prefix. For example, if bucket_folder is 'results/' and the path is 'my-results/file.txt', the code incorrectly treats it as already prefixed and returns it unchanged, skipping the necessary path resolution. This breaks the fix for issue #20174 in edge cases where folder names contain the bucket_folder as a substring.

issues.title: Incorrect parameter name prevents timeout configuration in test harness
issues.description: The test fixture uses `server_timeout=60` when calling `prefect_test_harness()`, but the correct parameter name is `server_startup_timeout`. This means the intended 60-second timeout is not actually applied, leaving tests vulnerable to the same timeout issues in CI environments that the change was meant to fix. The prefect_test_harness function will ignore the invalid parameter and use its default timeout value instead, potentially causing intermittent test failures when multiple xdist workers start simultaneously in CI.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Increase timeout for CI environments where multiple xdist workers
# start servers simultaneously, which can be slower on Python 3.11+
# See https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/issues/16397
with prefect_test_harness(server_timeout=60):
    yield

issues.title: Test constructs invalid path with double slashes
issues.description: The test constructs `already_prefixed_path = f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"` but bucket_folder always ends with a trailing slash (enforced by the _bucket_folder_suffix validator). This creates paths like 'results//abc123' with double slashes. While the double-nesting prevention logic should handle this, the test no longer accurately simulates the actual scenario described in issue #20174 where paths are already correctly prefixed without double slashes. This makes the test less effective at catching regressions in the double-nesting prevention logic.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Simulate path that already has bucket_folder prefix
# (as would happen when create_result_record calls _resolve_path)
already_prefixed_path = f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"

# When write_path calls _resolve_path again, it should NOT double-nest
result = gcs_bucket._resolve_path(already_prefixed_path)

issues.title: Unused import: model_validator
issues.description: `model_validator` is imported but not used anywhere in the modified code (the cross-field validation still uses `@field_validator`). This leaves an unused import in the module.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: from pydantic import Field, field_validator, model_validator
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20177 - fix(prefect-gcp): prevent double-nesting in GcsBucket._resolve_path

structured_output.summary:
The PR is meant to stop `GcsBucket._resolve_path` from adding `bucket_folder` twice when a path already carries it (issue #20174). It also changes the test harness timeout, fixes the `.prefectignore` fixture, and edits pytest warning filters. The goal is right, but the code doesn't carry it out.

The guard uses a substring check (`bucket_folder in path`) where it should use `startswith`, as `_join_bucket_folder` does. Any path that merely contains the folder name, like `archive/results/x` or `myresults/x`, skips the prefix, so files get written outside the configured folder. The regression test can't catch this: it builds a path with a double slash, which `_resolve_path` never produces, and its second assertion always passes. On top of that, `conftest.py` calls `prefect_test_harness(server_timeout=60)`, but the parameter is named `server_startup_timeout`. That session-scoped autouse fixture will raise `TypeError` and error out the whole prefect-gcp test suite. The PR also adds an unrelated validator that rejects `bucket_folder == bucket`, which breaks existing saved blocks, and it leaves `model_validator` imported but unused.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The test harness call uses the wrong keyword argument, so every prefect-gcp test errors at setup. The core fix uses a substring check that writes data to the wrong location. The regression test is too weak to catch either problem, and the new validator breaks existing blocks.

architecture.overview:
`GcsBucket` is the GCS storage block. Its `_resolve_path` helper joins the configured `bucket_folder` with a caller-supplied key. It's used by `write_path`, `read_path`, `get_directory` and `put_directory`. A separate helper, `_join_bucket_folder`, does the same job for the blob/folder-listing APIs and already guards against double-prefixing with `startswith` (from #18237). When the result-persistence layer has already resolved a storage key through the block (because `storage_block_id` is null), `write_path` resolves it again and the folder appears twice.

This PR adds an early return to `_resolve_path` when the path is judged to already include `bucket_folder`. It also adds a cross-field check to the `bucket_folder` field validator and changes test infrastructure: the harness timeout, the conftest logging fixture, warning filters, and the `.prefectignore` fixture.
steps: Start with `GcsBucket._resolve_path` (cloud_storage.py ~715). Every path-based read and write goes through it: `write_path`, `read_path`, `get_directory`, `put_directory`.
Look at the new early-return guard (line 734) and compare it with the existing `_join_bucket_folder` guard (line 928), which uses `startswith`.
Review the `_bucket_folder_suffix` validator change (lines 698-713). It now reads `info.data['bucket']` and rejects folders that match the bucket name.
Check `tests/conftest.py`. The session-wide `prefect_db` fixture now calls `prefect_test_harness` with a new keyword, and the `disable_logging` fixture has been removed.
Finally, look at the new regression test `test_resolve_path_no_double_nesting` and the `.prefectignore` fixture fix in `tests/projects/test_steps.py`.

diagrams.description: How a key flows through `_resolve_path` after this PR.

findings.title: `prefect_test_harness` called with a nonexistent `server_timeout` kwarg
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/conftest.py` line 19, `prefect_test_harness(server_timeout=60)` uses a keyword that doesn't exist. The real parameter, defined in `src/prefect/testing/utilities.py:114`, is `server_startup_timeout`. Change the call to `prefect_test_harness(server_startup_timeout=60)`. Also restore the removed session-scoped autouse `disable_logging` fixture, which wraps `temporary_settings({PREFECT_LOGGING_TO_API_ENABLED: False})`, along with its import, unless the removal was intentional.

findings.title: Substring check in `_resolve_path` skips the prefix for unrelated paths
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py` line 734, `_resolve_path` uses `self.bucket_folder in path` (a substring check) to detect an existing prefix. Any path that contains the folder name anywhere, e.g. `archive/results/x`, then skips the prefix and is written to the wrong location. Change it to `path.startswith(self.bucket_folder)` to match the existing guard in `_join_bucket_folder` (line 928). Then add tests asserting that `_resolve_path('other/base_folder/x')` and `_resolve_path('xbase_folder/y')` still get the prefix.

findings.title: Unrelated validator rejects existing blocks where `bucket_folder` equals the bucket name
findings.body:
This PR adds a new validation rule that has nothing to do with double-nesting:

::diff{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py" lines="698-713"}

Problems:
- **Breaking change**: a folder named after the bucket (e.g. `bucket="data"`, `bucket_folder="data"`) is a perfectly valid GCS layout. Any saved block with that config will now fail on `GcsBucket.load(...)`, which breaks existing deployments and result storage.
- The inline comment says the code *"should use @model_validator but incorrectly uses @field_validator"*, so it's knowingly wrong. It also depends on `bucket` being declared before `bucket_folder` to show up in `info.data`.
- `model_validator` is imported at line 10 but never used, which will fail ruff's F401 lint.

I'd drop this rule entirely, revert the signature to `(cls, value)`, and remove the unused import.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/prefect_gcp/cloud_storage.py`, remove the cross-field check added to `_bucket_folder_suffix` (lines ~698-713). It rejects valid configs where `bucket_folder` equals the bucket name, which breaks loading of existing saved blocks, and it's unrelated to the double-nesting fix. Restore the validator signature to `(cls, value)` and remove the unused `model_validator` import on line 10.

findings.title: Regression test uses an unrealistic path and an assertion that can't fail
findings.body:
::diff{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/test_cloud_storage.py" lines="156-165"}

- `bucket_folder` always ends with `/`, so `f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"` gives `"base_folder//abc123"`. `_resolve_path` never produces that; the realistic first-pass output is `"base_folder/abc123"`.
- `assert not result.startswith(f"{bucket_folder}{bucket_folder}")` is redundant after `result == already_prefixed_path`, so it can never fail on its own.
- No test covers the negative case, so the substring bug above passes unnoticed.

A stronger test makes the double call explicit and checks the negative case:

::suggestion{file="src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/test_cloud_storage.py" lines="156-165"}
        once = gcs_bucket._resolve_path("abc123")
        assert once == f"{bucket_folder}abc123"
        assert gcs_bucket._resolve_path(once) == once
        # paths merely containing the folder name must still be prefixed
        assert gcs_bucket._resolve_path(f"other/{bucket_folder}x") == f"{bucket_folder}other/{bucket_folder}x"
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/integrations/prefect-gcp/tests/test_cloud_storage.py`, `test_resolve_path_no_double_nesting` (lines 143-165) builds `f"{bucket_folder}/abc123"`. Since `bucket_folder` already ends with '/', that produces a double slash `_resolve_path` never emits, and the second assertion is redundant. Rewrite the test to: (1) call `_resolve_path('abc123')`, (2) assert that calling `_resolve_path` again on that result returns it unchanged, and (3) add a negative case showing a path that contains the folder name somewhere other than the start (e.g. `other/base_folder/x`) still gets prefixed.

findings.title: `.prefectignore` fixture fix is correct
findings.body:
The old triple-quoted string wrote indented lines, `    testdir1/*`, so those patterns didn't match what was intended. Writing `"testdir1/*\n.prefectignore\n"` makes the `push_to_gcs` ignore test actually exercise the ignore logic.
